items.title: Library supplement: Integration by parts on a finite product of unit spheres

source.attribution: Generic exposition of classical sphere calculus; no primary-textbook completion or novelty claim.

items.statement: For arbitrary \(n,N\in\mathbb N\), let \(E=\mathbb R^{n+1}\), \(S=\{x\in E:\|x\|=1\}\) and \(M=S^{\operatorname{Fin}N}\). Equip \(S\) with its induced Euclidean metric and stereographic smooth structure, and equip \(M\) with their product structures and the normalized polar product measure \(\mu=\sigma^{\otimes N}\) defined below. For every intrinsically C¹ real function \(f\) on \(M\) and every family of intrinsically C¹ maps \(V_i:M\to E\) satisfying \(\langle x_i,V_i(x)\rangle=0\) at every configuration and coordinate, all three displayed integrands are integrable and the following identities hold. The operators are the actual tangent gradient and tangent divergence, specified through canonical radial extension; their regularity and intrinsic interpretation are proved internally.
assumptions: \(n,N\in\mathbb N\) are arbitrary, with no positivity restriction. Thus the ambient dimension is \(n+1\); \(n=0\) gives the two-point sphere and \(N=0\) gives a one-point empty product.

The scalar field is \(\mathbb R\). All norms, inner products, tangent projections and manifold metrics are induced by the Euclidean structure. Regularity means regularity in the usual stereographic sphere charts and their finite product charts.

The reference measure is exactly \(\mu=\sigma^{\otimes N}\), with \(\sigma=\tau(S)^{-1}\tau\) and \(\tau=\operatorname{vol}_E.\mathrm{toSphere}\). Its finite nonzero mass and probability normalization are proved internally; they are not extra inputs.
For every supplied \(f:M\to\mathbb R\), assume \(f\in C^1(M)\). For every supplied family \(V_i:M\to E\), assume each \(V_i\in C^1(M;E)\), jointly in the complete configuration.

Tangency holds at every configuration and every coordinate: \(\langle x_i,V_i(x)\rangle=0\) for all \(x\in M\) and \(i\in\operatorname{Fin}N\). This is a pointwise hypothesis, not an almost-everywhere substitute.

formulae.label: Integration by parts on a finite product of unit spheres
formulae.tex: \begin{gathered}\operatorname{div}_M V,\quad f\operatorname{div}_M V,\quad\sum_{i\in\operatorname{Fin}N}\langle\nabla_i f,V_i\rangle\in L^1(\mu),\\\int_M\operatorname{div}_M V\,d\mu=0,\\\int_Mf\operatorname{div}_M V\,d\mu=-\int_M\sum_{i\in\operatorname{Fin}N}\langle\nabla_i f,V_i\rangle\,d\mu.\end{gathered}

obligations.label: Integration by parts on a finite product of unit spheres

bindings.boundary: This is a static integration identity for the specified normalized polar measure and its finite product. It gives no derivative in time, entropy evolution, diffusion existence, or density PDE. Identifying another supplied measure, gradient, divergence, or model generator with these definitions is a separate application obligation. The proof derives the required radial regularity from the intrinsic hypotheses. It neither assumes nor asserts that the totalized radial extension is continuous or differentiable at the origin. All integrals are ordinary finite real integrals. The conclusions include integrability, and no almost-everywhere-in-time or finite-horizon convention is involved. The zero-dimensional sphere and empty product are included. The proof retains the radial factor \(r^n/r\) on positive radii; it does not replace the exponent by truncated natural subtraction. The stated regularity is classical C¹/C². No weak-gradient, Sobolev, nonsmooth-weight, or arbitrary-measure extension is claimed.
